subject: docs/coop/artifacts/deferral.windows-platform.preview.v2.json
reviewClass: independent, refute not confirm; D-001/D-002 explicit-deferral candidate for a platform, not a register row
summary: This is the one candidate whose subject is a platform rather than a register row, and it handles that difference correctly: registerRow reads 'D-002 platform set — Windows' rather than naming a file-08 row, and the condition-2 effect says in terms that it neither adds nor removes a file-08 row and satisfies no gate. The four-platform set matches D-002 exactly, the re-entry clause routes a Windows-adding slice to a D-002 successor with its own review, and the refusal of silent Rosetta substitution matches D-006's standing prohibition.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: e7dd2b718fc6af5e46fc4706bc8b232a63c26beed4db42ec79a395b01af22b20, three measurements at the start and two at the close, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- throughout. The prompt held at 6a46241c… across start and end.

The commission is D-002's own, quoted accurately in both halves. D-002 reads 'Platforms: macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, arm64). Windows deferred with explicit disposition', and its explicit-deferrals paragraph lists 'Windows platform support' among the items each getting a recorded disposition. The artifact's four-platform list — macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, Linux x86_64, Linux arm64 — matches element for element with no fifth admitted and none dropped.

The attack 'treats Windows deferral as a file-08 row SATISFIED' fails, and the artifact is careful about a distinction the other four do not have to make. Its registerRow field reads 'D-002 platform set — Windows' rather than naming a row, and its condition-2 effect reads 'May count as the explicit preview platform deferral D-002 requires. Does not add or remove a file-08 row. Does not SATISFY any gate.' So it claims no row status at all, which is right: Windows is not a DR row, and a platform deferral that implied one would be inventing register structure.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails on the same clause plus the standing fields: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.

The deferral bounds itself in time. The reentry clause states that a later slice adding Windows 'is a D-002 successor for the platform set, with its own D-000 review' and that 'This deferral does not cover that slice', so recording it cannot be read as settling the platform set permanently — it names the successor route instead.

The Rosetta refusal matches a standing prohibition rather than being invented here. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled includes 'Silent Rosetta or non-Windows substitution as a Windows result', which is the same discipline D-006 imposes on the macOS x86_64 runner class — 'native Intel-class hardware, never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon', with unprocurability routed through a successor decision and 'never silent Rosetta substitution'. Applying that shape to Windows is consistent with the adopted rule.

The attack 'pulls deferred surface into preview' fails: whatMayBeDesigned admits only the four D-002 platform surfaces, and the exclusion list holds Windows as a preview-supported platform, a Windows DR-G01..G22 harness, and substitution results outside.

The claim that preview gates and harness identifiers bind only the four platforms is consistent with the register as D-088 left it. The gate rows carry harness identifiers and matrix descriptions without naming Windows, and D-006 bound its numeric thresholds to 'the D-002 slice's platforms (macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/arm64)'. Nothing in the artifact extends a gate to Windows or claims a Windows runner exists.

The attack 'coordinator pretending to be owner' fails. ownerWhoMustRecord reads 'Product + release + platform owners. Coordinator may draft', the effect is conditional throughout — condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded — and reversibility is 'Total before owner recording'. This candidate names no file-08 owner cell to check against, correctly, since the subject is a platform set rather than a row; the owner is named by role as D-002 assigns platform scope.

The attacks 'authorizing implementation', 'amending D-002' and 'file 08 edited' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses all three by name, opening with 'Does not amend D-002's four-platform set', which is the precise overreach available to a platform deferral. It also refuses to pin G03/G04 machines, which is the adjacent D-006 act a platform disposition could be mistaken for. file 08 measures 45dc4611… unmodified in my working tree.

The attack 'stale recordedInputs' fails. COORD 4ec06988… and file 08 45dc4611… both equal live bytes at the start and again at the close, and the remeasuredAfter marker f7ce35ff… resolves to 'D-093: record committed host-effect-authorization.v8 candidate'.
The frozen v1 predecessor is unedited: deferral.windows-platform.preview.v1.json hashes 5a28f0862a7a260a6459ca7a3b41ca18c95e7f48a56385c589b0a860cddc2d08, matching predecessorSha256.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

Whether any gate's platform matrix would in practice require a Windows runner. I verified the artifact claims none and that D-006 bound its thresholds to the four D-002 platforms; I did not audit all twenty-two gate matrix descriptions for an implicit Windows dependency.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of all five subjects and the prompt three times at the start and twice at the close, with ls -l for permissions; extraction and whitespace-unwrapping of D-002's Platforms and explicit-deferrals paragraphs from COORD for element-by-element comparison of the four-platform set; extraction of D-006's reference-runner-class paragraph for the Rosetta prohibition; inspection of file 08's gate rows for any Windows reference; sha256 of the frozen v1 predecessor; git log at full hash for the remeasuredAfter commit

acceptNote: ACCEPT at zero blockers and zero advisories. The structural risk unique to this candidate is that a platform is not a register row, so a disposition written in row-shaped language could imply a file-08 status that does not exist. It avoids that in the two places it could have gone wrong — registerRow names the D-002 platform set rather than a DR number, and the condition-2 effect states outright that nothing is added to or removed from file 08 and no gate is satisfied. The re-entry clause routes a future Windows slice to a D-002 successor under its own review rather than leaving the platform set looking closed.
